title: 2D hybrid steady-state magnetic field model for linear induction motors

source.citation: S. R. Aleksandrov, T. T. Overboom, E. A. Lomonova, Mathematical and Computational Applications 24(3):74, 2019
source.access: open access (CC BY 4.0); the PDF is cached locally (supplied for this replication)

related.citation: T. Overboom, J. Smeets, J. Jansen, E. Lomonova, Decoupled control of thrust and normal force in a double-layer single-sided linear induction motor, Mechatronics 23:213-221, 2013 (ref. [14])
related.use: The test rig and winding; not cached, not fetched.

related.citation: H. Bolton, Transverse edge effect in sheet-rotor induction motors, Proc. IEE 116:725-731, 1969 (ref. [18])
related.use: The plate conductivity's edge-effect reduction; not cached, not fetched.

machine.topology: linear, single-sided flat: a finite slotted primary (moving) over an infinitely long aluminium plate on solid back iron
machine.symmetry: None along x (a finite primary with end effects): the whole primary in a periodic domain of tau_per = 576 mm, A = 0 far above and below, as the paper's FEA. Standstill (slip 1): one time-harmonic solve per frequency.

components_map.part: slotted primary core (16 open slots, 10 mm end teeth, 8 mm end slots, two layers per slot)
double-layer winding (12 coils of 57 turns, coil pitch 2 slots) as Fig. 1 labels it
aluminium plate, back iron (with a fine skin layer), air gap and air
periodic ends of every layer and the distant A = 0 boundaries

turns_per_coil.quote: Number of turns per coil Nt 57
turns_per_coil.note: Each of the 12 coils drawn in Fig. 1 (a side in each layer) has 57 turns.

stack_width_mm.note: The model's depth: forces are per 50 mm of stack, as the paper's are.

slot_width_mm.note: Open rectangular slots (Figs. 1-2), filled by the coils.

slot_height_mm.note: Two equal layers of 10 mm, one coil side each (Figs. 1, 2 and 5).

air_gap_mm.note: From the teeth tips to the aluminium plate (Fig. 2).

plate_thickness_mm.quote: Thickness of the aluminum plate h Al 2 mm

back_iron_mm.quote: Thickness of the back-iron plate hbi 8 mm

al_conductivity_MS_per_m.note: Table 1's parameters are those 'used for both simulations' (p. 8), and the text says the plate's conductivity 'was reduced accordingly' for the transverse edge effect, citing Bolton [18]: 17 MS/m is read as the reduced value the FEA used (a 6000-series plate of about 25 MS/m times a Russell-Norsworthy factor of 0.70 gives 17.5). The further correction is a control (transverse_edge_factor).

iron_conductivity_MS_per_m.note: The solid back iron of the secondary.

iron_mu_r.note: Linear iron (the table prints the unit mm), for the laminated primary and the solid back iron alike.

primary_conductivity_MS_per_m.note: The primary is laminated, so no eddy currents flow in it (the paper's MEC region has none either).

peak_current_A.note: Peak phase current, as FEMM's phasors are.

phase_b_deg.note: I_B = I_p exp(-j 2 pi/3) exp(j 2 pi f t) (read from the page image).

phase_c_deg.note: I_C = I_p exp(+j 2 pi/3) exp(j 2 pi f t).

period_pole_pitches.note: The periodic length of both the hybrid model and the FEA, in pole pitches (24 slot pitches here); control period-528.

slots_per_pole.figure: Figs. 1 and 2 (winding labels) and Fig. 2's tau_1 arrow
slots_per_pole.note: The labels repeat A+, C-, B+, A-, C+, B- every six slots (one slot per pole and phase), and Fig. 2's tau_1 arrow spans three slot pitches (63.70 pt = 48.0 mm at the drawing's 1.3271 pt/mm). Table 1's 'fundamental pitch' of 12 mm cannot be this: see the gaps.

end_tooth_width_mm.figure: Fig. 2, p. 3 (vector drawing, to scale along x): the primary outline (69 vertices)
end_tooth_width_mm.scale_reference: slot pitch 16 mm (21.233 pt), checked by the 10 mm slots, 6 mm teeth and 48 mm tau_1 arrow (each within 0.011 mm)
end_tooth_width_mm.note: Full-height iron from each end of the primary to its first or last slot (a yoke overhang down to the tooth tips). Fig. 1 draws the same outline (266.0 mm at its own scale). The drawings' y is schematic (slot 24, yoke 10 and gap 8 mm drawn), their x to scale. Control ends-regular.

end_slot_width_mm.figure: Fig. 2, p. 3 (vector drawing, to scale along x): the primary outline
end_slot_width_mm.note: The first and last slots (empty in Fig. 1) are 8 mm wide, the other fourteen 10 mm.

gap_layer_current_sign.figure: Figs. 1 and 2 (winding labels) with Table 1's turns per coil
gap_layer_current_sign.note: Each label names a coil: the coil in the yoke-side layer of slot k returns in the gap-side layer of slot k + 2, where the drawing repeats its name, so that conductor carries the opposite current (-1 times the drawn sign). Read as conductor directions instead (+1, control conductor-reading), the two layers' currents would lie 120 electrical degrees apart (winding factor 0.5) instead of 60 (0.866). Decided before freezing by the pre-solve estimate (gaps).

transverse_edge_factor.reason: No further transverse edge-effect correction: Table 1's conductivity is the reduced one both simulations used. The paper gives neither the secondary width nor its correction factor.

air_height_mm.reason: Air above the primary and below the back iron, closed by A = 0 (the paper's Dirichlet boundary at y = +-infinity); the slowest harmonic of the 576 mm period decays 5e-3 over it. Control air-300.

dc_limit_frequency_hz.reason: The 0 Hz point of Fig. 9 is the AC solution's limit (the time average of a field travelling infinitely slowly): solved at 1 mHz, where the plate's eddy currents change the field by about 1e-5. A static solve would give one instant instead (comparator normal_t0_N).

back_iron_skin_mm.reason: The back iron's top 2 mm carries the fine mesh: the skin depth is 0.75 mm at 100 Hz (mu_r 1000, 4.5 MS/m) and 3.4 mm at 5 Hz.

gap_mesh_mm.reason: Air-gap elements: eight across the 2.7 mm gap.

plate_mesh_mm.reason: Plate elements: five across 2 mm (the skin depth is 12 mm at 100 Hz).

skin_mesh_mm.reason: Back-iron skin layer: three elements per skin depth at 100 Hz.

back_iron_mesh_mm.reason: The rest of the back iron.

field_line_spacing_mm.reason: Samples along the mid-gap line, 2112 over Figs. 6-7's 528 mm window (the paper's curves have vertices every 0.5 mm).

pole_pitch_mm.note: tau_1 = 48 mm: three slot pitches, as Fig. 2's arrow and Eq. (30) with Case 2 (10 m/s at 154.1667 Hz is a 50 Hz slip only for 2 tau_1 = 96 mm) both give.

primary_start_mm.note: The primary is centred on x = 0, as Figs. 6-7 show it in their 528 mm window.

field_line_y_mm.note: The middle of the air gap (Figs. 6 and 7).

gaps.item: Table 1's 'fundamental pitch of the primary' (12 mm)
gaps.affects: the period of the FE domain only
gaps.note: tau_1 is the pole pitch, 48 mm: three 16 mm slot pitches (the labels repeat every six slots), Fig. 2's tau_1 arrow (48.0 mm at the drawing's scale), Eq. (30) with Case 2 (154.1667 - 50 Hz = 10 m/s / (2 tau_1)), the text's sixth field harmonic as the fundamental and K = 576 MEC elements over tau_per (1 mm each). 12 mm cannot be built: tau_per = 144 mm would be shorter than the 266 mm primary. The period moves the forces by under 1e-5 in the pre-solve estimate; control period-528.

gaps.item: what the winding labels of Figs. 1-2 denote
gaps.affects: every force and field, by a factor of about two
gaps.note: Each layer shows A+, C-, B+, A-, C+, B- twice, the gap-side row two slots after the yoke-side one. Read as conductor directions, the two layers' currents lie 120 electrical degrees apart and the winding factor is 0.5; read as coil names (the coil in the yoke-side layer of slot k returns in the gap-side layer of slot k + 2, a short-pitched double layer with q = 1 and twelve coils of 57 turns), they lie 60 degrees apart (0.866). The pre-solve estimate (coarse finite differences, literal Table 1 inputs, no fitting) gives, under the coil reading, -75.0/-73.5, -46.5 and -24.1 N normal force at 0, 50 and 100 Hz (Fig. 9's FEA: -77.8, -47.6, -24.2) and 19.8-20.0 and 22.1-22.3 N thrust at 50 and 100 Hz (20.4, 22.5), and reproduces Figs. 6-7 point by point in shape, sign and size; under the conductor reading it gives -60, -18 and -7.6 N and 9.3 and 8.9 N. The coil reading is frozen (gap_layer_current_sign -1), the conductor reading is control conductor-reading.

gaps.item: the plate's conductivity and the transverse edge effect (secondary width not given)
gaps.affects: thrust and normal force with frequency
gaps.note: Table 1's 17 MS/m is read as the reduced value both simulations used (transverse_edge_factor 1). Bracketed before freezing: treating it as the raw conductivity and applying a Russell-Norsworthy factor (0.695 for a 100 mm plate) lowers the thrust 17% and raises the normal force 18% at 50 Hz and 48% at 100 Hz in the pre-solve estimate; control russell-norsworthy. Bolton's correction [18], which the paper cites, is not cached and was not fetched.

gaps.affects: end effects, the normal force at low frequency
gaps.note: Read from Fig. 2's outline, to scale along x: 10 mm end teeth (full height) and 8 mm end slots. Under 0.1% in the pre-solve estimate; control ends-regular.

gaps.item: the FE domain: periodic length and the distant boundaries
gaps.note: Periodic in x over tau_per = 12 tau_1 = 576 mm, as the text gives for both models; A = 0 at 150 mm above the primary and below the back iron for the paper's Dirichlet boundary at infinity. Figs. 6-7 span 528 mm with the primary at their centre (the pre-solve estimate lines up), so the field targets use rms over that window, which does not depend on the period; controls period-528 and air-300.

gaps.item: the field plots: component and instant
gaps.note: Fig. 6's axis reads Bx and its caption 'normal'; Fig. 7's axis By and its caption 'longitudinal'. The axis labels are taken: the pre-solve estimate's B_x and B_y at the middle of the gap, as phasor real parts at t = 0 under Eqs. (1)-(3) with '+' conductors along +z, match Figs. 6 and 7 in shape and sign. Comparators label 'caption' hold the other reading.

Under Eqs. (1)-(3) and Fig. 1 the current sheet's phase falls 60 degrees per slot along +x, so the field travels toward the front end and pushes the primary toward the rear end (-x); the text says the propulsion on the primary is along +x and Fig. 9 plots it positive, while Figs. 6-7 (above) follow the drawing's frame. The metric is the propulsion, -F_x.
The AC solution's limit (time average), as for the other frequencies; solved at 1 mHz. The instant t = 0 is comparator normal_t0_N@f000.

gaps.item: the FE tool and its mesh
gaps.note: Not named; a mesh study (mesh-0p75, mesh-1p4) bounds the model's own discretization.

gaps.item: Case 2 (v = 10 m/s) and Fig. 10's harmonic decomposition
gaps.note: FEMM's time-harmonic solver has no velocity term; Fig. 10 is the hybrid model's Fourier decomposition.
The paper reports only that the models agree within 3.1%, without a value.

measurements.note: Time-averaged x force on the whole primary (iron, coils and slot air): weighted stress tensor.
J x B on the plate's eddy currents alone (diagnostic: the back iron's share is not in it).
2112 points every 0.25 mm along the middle of the gap, over Figs. 6-7's 528 mm window centred on the primary.

metrics.name: thrust_N
metrics.note: Propulsion: the force on the primary opposite to the travelling field (which moves toward +x, the front end, under Eqs. (1)-(3) and Fig. 1), so -F_x in the drawing's frame; the paper plots it positive.

metrics.name: normal_N
metrics.note: F_y on the primary; negative is attraction toward the secondary.

metrics.name: normal_t0_N
metrics.note: The normal force at t = 0 (i_A = I_p): the mean plus the double-frequency part's real part.

controls.purpose: Every explicit element size at 0.75 times (about 1.8 times the elements).
Every explicit element size at 1.4 times: the coarse side of the mesh study.

The labels as conductor directions: the gap-side layer carries its drawn sign, 120 electrical degrees from the yoke-side layer (pre-solve estimate: thrust -55%, normal force -23% at 0 Hz and -62% at 50 Hz).

Table 1's 17 MS/m read as the plate's own conductivity, reduced by the Russell-Norsworthy factor for a 100 mm wide plate (25 mm overhang each side of the 50 mm stack; tau 48 mm): 1 - tanh(ka)/(ka (1 + tanh(ka) tanh(k c'))) = 0.6953 with k = pi/tau, a = 25 mm, c' = 25 mm (pre-solve estimate: thrust -17%, normal force +18% at 50 Hz).
A 528 mm period, the window Figs. 6-7 draw with the primary at its centre (pre-solve estimate: forces unchanged to 5 digits).
A = 0 twice as far above and below.
Regular end teeth and end slots instead of the drawing's 10 and 8 mm (a 262 mm primary; pre-solve estimate: under 0.1%).

coverage.reproduced: The 2D FEA thrust and normal force from 0 to 100 Hz at standstill (Fig. 9, 41 acceptance values) and the mid-gap flux density components at 100 Hz (Figs. 6-7, rms over the plotted window); the hybrid model's and the measured forces and the text's 20.4 N as comparators.
coverage.not_reproduced: The moving case (Case 2, v = 10 m/s: FEMM has no velocity term), Fig. 10's harmonic decomposition and the Joule losses (no value given); the transverse edge effect is in the plate's reduced conductivity, as in the paper.
